question: Obtain the equation of the normal to the curve $y=\sin x$ at the origin. Verify that it is perpendicular to the tangent at that point.
explanation: Slope of the tangentFor $y=\sin x$,$$\frac{dy}{dx}=\cos x$$At the origin, $x=0$, so$$m_t=\cos0=1$$Slope of the normal$$m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-1$$Equation through the originThe normal passes through $(0,0)$. Hence,$$y-0=-1(x-0)$$$$y=-x$$Perpendicularity verification$$m_tm_n=(1)(-1)=-1$$Therefore, the tangent and normal are perpendicular.ConclusionThe equation of the normal is $x+y=0$.

options.D: $x=0$; the normal is parallel to the $y$-axis
